page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-96 is a high-memory compute instance featuring 96 vCPUs across 48 physical Intel Xeon cores clocked at 2.6 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with hyperthreading enabled, the instance provides 768.0 GB of total RAM, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache structures include 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 54 MB L3 cache pool. CPU instruction sets include AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark outcomes show distinct multi-core throughput and memory access performance. Multi-threaded evaluations such as the PassMark CPU test (74,382.22), Geekbench multi-core (17,004.0), and stress-ng multi-core (89,966.98) place this machine in the top tier of compute capacity. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 333.34 GB/sec for 256 MB reads and 144.43 GB/sec for writes, scaling up to 4,896.56 GB/sec for cached 16 KB read blocks. Additionally, in-memory key-value processing achieves strong performance, demonstrated by 88.47 million Redis SET operations per second and 30,989.85 points in PassMark database operations.

Single-core performance presents a moderate profile. Stress-ng single-core (1,838.08), Geekbench single-core (1,571.0), and single-threaded gzip compression (27.69 GB/sec) score within average distributions. The configuration lacks local bundled NVMe storage and dedicated GPU accelerators, meaning network storage interfaces must be provisioned separately. For machine learning tasks, while small model inference prompt processing is strong, large language model text generation degrades to 2.51 tokens per second on 70B models due to the absence of dedicated matrix acceleration chips like AMX.

Given its massive memory allocation and multi-threaded throughput, the n2-highmem-96 configuration delivers efficient resource utilization for large-scale enterprise databases, distributed in-memory data grids, large Clang compilation workflows, and static high-throughput web serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-96 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 96 vCPUs across 48 physical Intel Xeon cores at 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 768.0 GB of RAM, it maintains an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, supported by a 54 MB L3 cache and AVX-512 VNNI instructions. The instance exhibits exceptional multi-core and memory subsystem performance, reaching 333.34 GB/sec in large-block uncached read memory bandwidth and processing 88.47 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core speeds remain average, and it includes no bundled local storage or dedicated GPUs. This configuration is best suited for in-memory databases, large-scale caching layers, data processing, and highly concurrent enterprise workloads requiring large memory capacities.
